# Working Notes: Marlowe & Pine Customer Support

## Reply format (all customer replies)
- If the account locale is not English, open the reply with a greeting in that language on the first line (for example Hola, Bonjour, Hallo, Olá). Use the locale field on the account, not the customer's name.
- End every reply with exactly two lines: `Warmly,` then `The Marlowe & Pine Crew`. No personal names or other closings.
- QA reviews replies separately from CI. QA approval is what clears a reply. A CI result alone does not.
- Never promise a delivery date, or a number of days, for when a parcel will arrive. Carriers move those dates and we own the miss. Give the tracking number and say the carrier has the latest estimate.
- For a refund, state the amount, the order number, and that the bank may take a few business days to show it. Say "refunded" only once the action log shows the refund.
- Never write that a refund or credit is approved, issued, or processing unless the action log shows it. Say it has been passed to the review team.

## Standard order of steps
1. Verify the customer and order. The action log must show `verify` with `ok: true` before any account or refund action.
2. Check the refund amount against the $40 limit and note the result in the case.
3. Run `refund` if the amount is at or under $40. If over $40, escalate instead (see below).
4. Run account changes (such as an email update) only after a passing verify. Confirm the change in the reply.
5. Write the reply, then tag and close the case.

## Case closing and tags
- Before closing any case, give it exactly one tag from: billing, shipping, product, account, other.
- Never add a second tag or a custom label, and never close a case with no tag. Reporting breaks on all three.
- Pick the tag by the main issue. If a case covers two areas, use the one the customer's main request is about and put the other in the case note.
- A missing item from a package is tagged `shipping`. QA approved this tag.
- A defective item that arrived broken is tagged `product`. QA approved the reply on this kind of case.

## Refund and credit policy
- Refunds at or under $40: within our authority. Run `refund`.
- Refunds over $40: do not run `refund`. Escalate with `desk.py escalate <case> finance-ops` and leave the decision to them. Finance-ops pays out; we do not.
- Goodwill credits and compensation have no documented limit. Do not promise or grant one. Escalate to `tier2` with the amount requested, the order, and the carrier status. Tell the customer the request is under review.
- A damage claim can have two parts (a refund and a goodwill credit). Escalate each to its own team, and say in the escalation note that the other part exists.
